To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the field of HDL-raising therapies has evolved substantially over the past 2 decades, and that the next generation of HDL-raiser will likely have multiple mechanisms of action, including upregulation of cholesterol efflux, inhibition of cholesterol absorption, and/or inhibition of CETP.

the HDL-cholesterol-raising drugs niacin, CETP inhibitors and apoA-I Milano-containing HDL are of uncertain clinical benefit, and that the HDL flux hypothesis may be more relevant than the HDL cholesterol hypothesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new therapies for atherosclerosis, with a particular interest in the role played by high-density lipoprotein (HDL) in atherogenesis.
the identification of novel targets for the prevention of cardiovascular disease.
the development and validation of new biomarker assays for the assessment of cardiovascular risk, and the development of new therapies to prevent and/or treat cardiovascular diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the field of HDL-raising therapies is at a crossroads, with many new agents under development.
HDL-C is not the only important factor in HDL biology, and that HDL-C should not be the only factor used to measure HDL function.
the field is still evolving, and that there are several promising therapeutic approaches that will likely be in the clinic in the near future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the field of HDL-raising therapies has evolved substantially over the past decade and is poised for further advances in the coming decade.
HDL is a complex and heterogeneous particle that plays a central role in atherogenesis and that HDL-raising therapies may be beneficial in the prevention of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.
HDL-raising therapies have been developed that raise HDL cholesterol concentrations by >50 % and that are in clinical development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the field has been greatly enriched by recent clinical trials and the identification of new targets and new HDL therapeutics.
HDL-C may be a useful surrogate marker for the efficacy of HDL therapies, but the HDL-C level itself does not appear to be a good predictor of cardiovascular risk.
the HDL-C hypothesis has been replaced by the HDL flux hypothesis.
